text:
The word around Pittsburgh is fire sale. Erik Karlsson trade rumors have Carolina interested, according to The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun, writers are asking what happens to Evgeni Malkin (the latest reporting has him expected to stay), and for the first time the conversation has reached Sidney Crosby, with columnists openly wondering whether the unthinkable is now thinkable. That is where a 7-11-2 start gets you.

The frustrating part is that the play is better than the record. The Penguins have taken 52% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), and our points model has them almost five points behind what their play has earned. They've scored about six fewer goals than their chances, and the power play produces only 0.44 expected goals a game, a real drag for a team with this much skill. Our playoff odds sit at 14%.

The crease is unsettled. Arturs Silovs is at .855 and 3.6 goals worse than expected over his last five starts. Sergei Murashov put on a show in a shootout win in San Jose, and he's the kind of young goalie a retooling team wants to see more of.

There are pieces that work: Crosby with Rickard Rakell and Tommy Novak, Malkin's line with Novak and Egor Chinakhov, Ben Kindel growing into a role. What we'd watch: the trade calls, because the next month decides whether this is a slump or a teardown.
